ip_top_stories.title: Meta and Anthropic win key verdicts in US AI copyright cases
ip_top_stories.summary: Meta and Anthropic have secured significant court victories in US AI copyright litigation. The outcomes are likely to shape the legal landscape for AI training on copyrighted material, with courts finding in favour of the AI companies on key claims.

ip_top_stories.title: Google Sued Over Alleged Use Of Copyrighted Music To Train Lyria 3 AI
ip_top_stories.summary: Google is facing a lawsuit from independent artists alleging it used copyrighted music without authorisation to train its Lyria AI music models on YouTube content. Google has cited YouTube's terms of service as a defence in the case. The lawsuit is being pursued as a class action and represents a significant test of AI training rights in the music industry.

ip_top_stories.title: 3rd Circuit Mulls Fair-Use Defense in Westlaw's Copyright Suit Against AI Startup
ip_top_stories.summary: The US Third Circuit Court of Appeals is weighing whether a fair-use defence applies in Thomson Reuters' copyright lawsuit against AI legal startup Ross Intelligence over use of Westlaw content to train its AI. Judges questioned Ross's arguments during oral arguments, signalling potential scepticism about the fair-use claim in this context.

ip_top_stories.title: Japan to Draw Up Rules to Protect Intellectual Property in AI Age
ip_top_stories.summary: Japan has announced plans to develop new regulations aimed at protecting intellectual property in the context of AI development and deployment. The move reflects growing government concern about the adequacy of existing IP frameworks as AI systems become more capable.

ip_top_stories.title: Dutch Court Artist Receives Damages Over Far-Right AI Image Alteration
ip_top_stories.summary: A Dutch court has awarded damages to an artist whose work was altered using AI to produce far-right imagery without consent. The ruling is notable as an early European judicial decision recognising artist rights in the context of AI-generated image manipulation.

ip_further_links.title: Google Will Appeal a German Ruling That Makes It Legally Liable When Its AI Overviews Lie
ip_further_links.summary: Google has said it will appeal a landmark German court ruling that found it legally liable for false information generated by its AI Overviews feature, with the court treating AI-generated answers as Google's own statements.

ip_further_links.title: You Think Your AI Content Is Protected. The Supreme Court Disagrees
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of US Supreme Court precedent finding that AI-generated content does not attract copyright protection, with implications for businesses and creators relying on AI tools.

ip_further_links.title: AI In the Public Interest: Authorship & Copyright in the Age of AI
ip_further_links.summary: A policy-focused discussion on the evolving questions around authorship and copyright as AI systems become capable of generating creative works, examining what the public interest requires from legal frameworks.

ip_further_links.title: How a small Canadian publisher is resisting the AI book wave
ip_further_links.summary: A report on how a small Canadian publishing house is pushing back against the use of AI in book production and taking a stance on AI training data rights.

ip_further_links.title: Paul Deegan: 'AI for All' must protect Canadian journalism copyright
ip_further_links.summary: News Media Canada CEO Paul Deegan argues that Canada's AI strategy must include robust protections for journalism copyright to ensure publishers are compensated when their content is used to train AI systems.

ip_further_links.title: AI Regulation and the Looming Problem of the Takings Clause
ip_further_links.summary: Legal analysis examining whether proposed AI regulations in the US could trigger Fifth Amendment takings clause claims from technology companies whose AI systems are restricted or curtailed by government action.

ip_further_links.title: Wolters Kluwer expands its Libra AI workspace with authoritative Swiss legal content from leading publisher Stampfli
ip_further_links.summary: Wolters Kluwer has announced a licensing agreement with Swiss publisher Stampfli to incorporate authoritative legal content into its Libra AI legal workspace platform.
